item.title: Saga Summer Gion Festival — Guide
item.description: Like many towns across Japan, Saga celebrates a summer Gion festival, a traditional Shinto festival held to pray for protection from plague and misfortune in the hot months. Rooted in centuries-old custom, Saga’s Gion festivities bring the streets to life with processions of tall, elaborately decorated festival floats, portable shrines (mikoshi) carried by teams of locals, and the beat of drums and chanting, often lit by lanterns as evening falls. The atmosphere is festive and communal, with crowds lining the route, food stalls, summer yukata and a real sense of local pride and tradition.
